message.content:
Here’s a concise overview of key traffic laws and regulations in Texas: | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• Speed limit enforcement uses radar, laser, and speed cameras. | | **Seat Belt Use** | • All drivers and front-seat passengers must wear seat belts.
• Back-seat passengers under 13 must use a child safety seat. | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited unless using a hands‑free device. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for all drivers.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers (0.04%) and drivers under 21 (0.02%). | | **Traffic Signal Compliance** | • Red lights require a full stop; green lights allow proceeding only if the intersection is clear.
• Yellow lights indicate caution; drivers should not enter the intersection if it would be unsafe. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right have priority.
• Pedestrians always have priority at crosswalks. | | **School Bus Laws** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus has its stop sign extended and red lights flashing.
• Stopping distance varies by vehicle size. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Drivers must stay within their lane unless turning or changing lanes.
• Lane changes require signaling and checking blind spots. | | **Use of Headlights** | • Headlights must be used from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather. | | **Towing Regulations** | • Towing vehicles must maintain a safe following distance and use proper towing equipment. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and pass an annual safety inspection.
• Emission inspections are required in certain counties. | | **Parking Restrictions** | • Parking on sidewalks, in front of driveways, or in designated no‑parking zones is prohibited.
• Parking meters and timed parking signs must be obeyed. | ### How to Stay Informed 1. **Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT)** – Offers up-to-date traffic law resources and driver education materials. 2. **Texas Motor Vehicle Commission (MVA)** – Provides registration, licensing, and inspection guidelines. 3. **Local County Courts** – For specific case law or recent rulings affecting traffic statutes. If you need more detailed information on a particular aspect—such as DUI penalties, toll roads, or specific county ordinances—just let me know!
